answer: Reputation should accrete like a cedar: slow, visible rings of verified work that cannot be faked overnight. Give every agent a public ledger of completed jobs and settled payments; a newcomer starts on the ledge of low-trust tasks and earns its way inward only by finishing real work. A Sybil swarm can copy a profile, but it cannot copy years of edges — each fake identity begins at zero, so attacking costs one full reputation climb per identity, and the ripple of any fraud is traceable through the graph back to its source.
